about: Hidden fishing spots picked by hand from public sources (park pages, regulations, published trip reports): hike-in, canoe-in or rough-road waters most anglers never reach. Edit by hand (tag: a few words on why it's quiet, shown on the map); the app shows them in the Hidden spots layer with the walk-in stocked lakes from data/fishing/walkin.json.

spots.how: Hike from the north end of Callaghan Lake; the road in needs a high-clearance vehicle (deep cross-ditches) and is snowed in about November to early June.
spots.tip: An alpine tarn at about 1,500 m, the biggest of several in the cirque. No dogs in the Cirque Lake basin (grizzly habitat).

spots.how: 8 km of rough forest road (high-clearance only) past the Callaghan Valley Road; shore or small boat, motors under 10 hp.
spots.tip: Subalpine lake at 1,200 m that most Whistler visitors drive past.

spots.how: About 9 km of trail from the Rubble Creek trailhead.
spots.tip: Stocked by hand in 1928-29 and never since; the trout are about 30 cm but plentiful. Fly fishing does well.

spots.how: Off-trail beyond Garibaldi Lake.
spots.tip: Hikers report even better fishing than the big lake.

spots.how: About 3 km of easy trail from the end of Cheakamus Lake Road, south of Whistler.
spots.tip: One of the fishing lakes BC Parks names in Garibaldi Park.

spots.how: A long backcountry trip past Elfin Lakes (Diamond Head trailhead, Squamish).
spots.tip: One of the fishing lakes BC Parks names in Garibaldi Park; very few people get this far.

spots.how: Hike-in only (no vehicles on the Lakeview road; check the road after the 2023 Crater Creek fire).
spots.tip: BC Parks: the best fishing in Cathedral Park. Fish are small (15-25 cm) but plentiful. Not stocked.

spots.how: Hike-in only, Cathedral Park core area.
spots.tip: Spawning trout show up at the outlet footbridge in the fall.

spots.how: Hike-in only, Cathedral Park core area.
spots.tip: Healthy wild trout; spawning fish at the outlet in the fall.

spots.how: Hike-in only, Cathedral Park core area.
spots.tip: Core-area lake with wild trout, not stocked.

spots.fish: Cutthroat trout (about 20 cm), Dolly Varden (about 30 cm)
spots.how: 6 km easy trail from the Nicol Creek trailhead, about 52 km up the White Swan and Lussier forest roads from Kimberley.
spots.tip: Bait ban, flies and lures only. Gently release dark-coloured trout from early June to July 15 (spawning).

spots.how: About 1 km walk from the Elk Lakes parking lot, at the end of a long forest road.
spots.tip: Best right after break-up and from September to freeze-up; poor in July-August run-off. No ice fishing.

spots.how: Developed trail past Lower Elk Lake.
spots.tip: Best right after break-up and in the fall. No ice fishing.

spots.how: Rough, less developed trail from the Cadorna Creek trailhead.
spots.tip: Few people make the trip.

spots.how: Rough, less developed trail.
spots.tip: Few people make the trip.

spots.how: Hike from Gibson Lake (16 km of rough road up Kokanee Creek from Hwy 3A).
spots.tip: Alpine lake, 1.2 km long. No campfires in the park.

spots.how: Hike past Kokanee Lake toward the Kokanee Glacier cabin.
spots.tip: One of the park's fishing lakes.

spots.how: Backcountry, Kokanee Glacier Park.
spots.tip: One of the park's fishing lakes.

spots.how: 6 km easy trail (about 2 h) from the Spectrum Creek parking lot, 16 km up a logging road.
spots.tip: Bigger fish than Peters Lake.

spots.how: 5 to 9 km of difficult trail past Spectrum Lake.
spots.tip: Lots of fish, smaller than Spectrum's.

spots.how: 4 km trail (about 90 minutes) near Mahood Lake, Wells Gray Park.
spots.tip: BC Parks: good fishing at the end of the trail.

spots.how: Paddle up Clearwater Lake (no launch on Azure), then a 0.5 km portage.
spots.tip: Try the lake ends and the creek mouths.

spots.fish: Rainbow, lake and bull trout, kokanee, whitefish
spots.how: Bowron Lake canoe circuit only (reservation needed, no motors).
spots.tip: Best in June and September; bring a mix of flies and lures.

spots.how: Steep trail from the Lantern Creek parking on Highway 40.
spots.tip: Four alpine lakes joined by small streams. Catch and release, bait ban, flies and lures only, open July 1 to October 31.

spots.how: About 4 km of trail from Upper Kananaskis Lake.
spots.tip: A hike-in lake anglers head to instead of the busy Kananaskis Lakes.

spots.how: About 5 km of trail off the Smith-Dorrien road.
spots.tip: A hike-in lake; the highest lakes hold the cutthroat.

spots.how: Hike in off Highway 40.
spots.tip: A hike-in lake few people fish.

spots.how: About 7 km of trail from Cameron Lake or Waterton townsite.
spots.tip: One of the few Waterton lakes where you may keep cutthroat (2 a day). National park fishing permit; open July 1 to October 31.

spots.how: High on the Carthew-Alderson trail, past Alderson Lake.
spots.tip: Native, colourful cutthroat; limit 2 a day. National park permit; July 1 to October 31.

spots.how: About 5.5 km of steep trail from Waterton townsite.
spots.tip: Cutthroat limit 2 a day. National park permit; July 1 to October 31.

spots.how: Boat shuttle across Waterton Lake, then about 9 km of trail (with a tunnel and a cable).
spots.tip: Cutthroat limit 2 a day. National park permit; July 1 to October 31.

spots.how: Off-trail route above Lineham Creek: experienced hikers only.
spots.tip: Cutthroat limit 2 a day. National park permit; July 1 to October 31.

spots.how: Backcountry, on the Tamarack trail.
spots.tip: Cutthroat limit 2 a day. National park permit; July 1 to October 31.

spots.how: About 1.2 km easy trail off the Akamina Parkway.
spots.tip: A short walk that keeps the crowds away. Open May 17 to September 1; National park permit.

spots.how: 45-minute trail rated very difficult; no ATVs. Sépaq boat on the lake.
spots.tip: Sépaq day fishing, book ahead; limit 10 brook trout.

spots.how: 90-minute walk from road 36 in the Mastigouche reserve (or 4x4); you can't bring your own boat.
spots.tip: Sépaq day fishing, book ahead.

spots.how: 1.7 km trail (ATV needed) in the Rouge-Matawin reserve.
spots.tip: Sépaq day fishing, book ahead.

spots.how: Canoe-in from the Shall Lake access point, Algonquin Park (portages).
spots.tip: Productive in spring for both trouts; over a dozen interior campsites. No live bait fish anywhere in Algonquin.
